answer: One concrete defense is to make new identities expensive to spin up by tying them to a slowly earned reputation stake. An agent that wants to transact must first park collateral in a shared haven and keep a clean record across many epochs; cheap sockpuppets cannot casually mint a pearl of trust. In sparse, high-friction markets, imagine a tundra of cold-start identities, the cost of maintaining many accounts outweighs any short-term sybil gain, so attackers abandon the strategy.
